about: A touchscreen: what it registers with (beside an e-paper screen's registration, the same route) and is answered, what GET /api/devices/config answers (a touchscreen is paired by token, so never has a pairing code), and what it saves with PUT /api/devices/config from its own settings panel (`save`: the whole config as it got it, its skin and sleep changed, read-only fields and all), what it saves a section at a time with PUT /api/devices/config/{section} (`section_save`: the section's name, the version it was changed from as If-Match, the section whole, and the config answered with its new version), and what GET /api/devices/spotify/token answers it once paired (`spotify_token`: an access token for its owner's Spotify), and what GET /api/devices/account answers it (`account`: which services its owner's account has linked, here Spotify but no Parcel key). Each of its people has their own Spotify Soloist API key, saved for the touchscreen with a code: what it asks POST /api/devices/soloist/codes for one of them and is answered (`soloist_code_request`, `soloist_code`), the query of the settings site's /soloist it shows as a link (`soloist_page`), what GET /api/devices/soloist/keys answers once they've saved it (`soloist_keys`), and what GET /api/devices/soloist/key answers for them (`soloist_key_query`, `soloist_key`). Its people sign in to Spotify on their phones: what it asks POST /api/devices/spotify/sign-ins with and is answered (`spotify_sign_in_request`, `spotify_sign_in`), the query of the settings site's /spotify/sign-in it shows as a code to scan (`spotify_sign_in_page`), the query Spotify sends the phone back to /spotify/sign-in/callback with (`spotify_sign_in_callback`), and what GET /api/devices/spotify/sign-ins/{id} answers before and after (`spotify_sign_in_waiting`, `spotify_sign_in_done`). It can register through the login instead, at the settings site's /register (`register`: the query it opens, with its secret's hash, and `registered_return` and `taken_return`, where the page sends it back to). The touchscreen's tests check its client against these, and the broker's tests its routes. An e-paper screen's config is config_store.json's. The store contract's canonical example (countdown-api's countdown_api/fixtures), which every consumer's tests read: change it there.
